answer: In PoA, each identity locks bonded collateral, while cryptographic evidence of coordinated equivocation groups k identities into one fault domain: aggregate penalties scale quadratically, O(k^2), and detection triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss against the controlling escrow. This asymmetric depreciation makes sybil expansion uneconomic, whether coordination spans a summit, an island, or a delta, because shared keys, timing, and payout paths expose linkage.
